coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Old Metal Dealers Act: dealer licence from Police Commander of division (G$40,000 in 2008), storage sites listed/inspected, export licence per shipment via commerce ministry plus Scrap Metal Unit inspection, minister power to ban exports up to 1 year. Sept 2026 warning: licence cancellation for handling illegal copper, possible full trade shutdown. See candidate C01.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbroking Act Cap 91:09 (books, pawn tickets, precious-metal pledges, surplus to public trustee). GRA pawn licence annual, G$25,000-50,000 by location, needs Magistrate's Court Money Lenders' Certificate and police clearance. No ongoing police reporting found. See C03. No second-hand dealer regime found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Only Guyana Gold Board dealer licence or GGMC trader licence may buy gold; goldsmiths must source raw gold from GGB. Dec 2025 MNR/GGDMA meeting: stricter audits of purchase records and source-declaration verification, rolled out immediately. See C02.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or spare-parts dealer licence found. Adjacent: GRA Dealer's General Licence (Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act s21), reconditioned-vehicle pre-shipment inspection certificate required from 1 Jan 2025. See C04.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: GLDA Act Cap 71:10 requires licence to trade/export livestock and livestock products; Slaughter of Cattle (Control) Act needs vet written approval for female/young cattle. No animal movement permit regime found. See C05.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Georgetown Abattoir By-Laws (register of slaughterers, slaughter licence); Onverwagt state abattoir charges butchers G$3,000 per animal (2026). Laws described as outdated by stakeholders. Folded into C05.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Pilot National Registration and Traceability System (GFSA with GLDA) registers apiarists, GPS-maps apiaries, QR-codes honey, under Food Safety Act 2019; registered beekeepers rose 160 to 213. State-run, tiny base. See C06.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinarians Act 2003 (Veterinary Board registers vets and animal health assistants); Government Analyst Dept programme to regularise import/sale of vet drugs; Act revision pending. No licence process for sellers confirmed. Very small base. See C07.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Hydromet Department licence required before drilling wells (Water and Sewerage Act 2002, Part V), after EPA clearance; well registration campaign (2017). See C08.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No septic hauler licence category found. EPA Water Quality Regulations require registration/authorisation for any discharge; EPA e-service for Environmental Authorisation live since 14 Oct 2025 (eservices.epa.gov.gy). Nothing new beyond K01 adjacency.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: OSH Dept registers workplaces (annual re-registration reported, undated) and issues steam boiler certificates (Steam Boilers Regulation Act Cap 95:04; OSH Act Cap 99:10 Part II). No lift or pressure-vessel regime found. ILO OSH Act reform project Mar 2026 to Jun 2027. See C09.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing found on community/small water system licensing beyond Guyana Water Inc and Hydromet licensing. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: PTCCB Act Cap 68:09: product registration, sell licence (s13), premises registration for storage (s14), licence for pest extermination for reward; roadside vending enforcement. Number of licensed dealers not found. See C10.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Recruiting of Workers Act Cap 98:06 licence plus security required; 2021 Labour Ministry register drive, agencies mostly unregistered, oil-sector linkage. See C11.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Funeral parlours only need registration with Central Board of Health under archaic Public Health Ordinance; reform proposals (annual licensing) from 2013 unconfirmed. Cemeteries run by councils. See C12.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Friendly Societies Act: annual returns to Registrar with audited accounts (older source); no new NPO law found. Halal/kosher not searched. See C13.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Road service licence under Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act Cap 51:02; 2019 minibus code (association membership, uniforms, training); May 2026 Public Works Minister warned of licence suspension for fare gouging and ordered approved fares displayed. Nothing new beyond K08.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: M&CC street vending policy and vendor registration repeatedly announced (draft policy reported 2021 and again Jan 2025); no confirmed adopted licence. Money changers covered by K03. See C14.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childcare and Development Services Regulations in force 4 May 2016; CPA registration then licence, with fire, CH&PA and public health inspections; 2026 MHSSS: 352 licensed, 376 registered facilities. GFSA licenses food business operators and handlers' permits under Food Safety Act 2019 (amendment under way). Tattoo studios, driving schools, hunting outfitters: nothing found. See C15, C16.

Food and Drugs Regulations 2012 cover controlled-drug prescription records. A new Medicines Regulation Bill is drafted and a pharmacovigilance system is being built (PAHO 2026), so rules may change. Candidate C08 (weak/unverified).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private Security Services Act (2009; bill text seen, enacted text not confirmed): Commissioner of Police licenses security agencies, annual licence and renewal, register and accounts to be kept by agencies, guard ID cards; firms also need NIS registration. Calls for a sector audit in 2023. No count of firms and no local guard-management software found. Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Local-content reporting is already in K01/K02. Small-scale mining: President ordered in Jan 2026 that all gold produced in 2025 be declared and that dredges with no declaration be deregistered; miners must be registered with the Ministry and hold a local bank account. GGMC declaration is in person at offices or visiting days; no digital system mentioned. Candidate C04.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: FIU table: Guyana Compliance Commission supervises attorneys, commissioners of oaths, accountants and auditors (appointed 16/08/2023); Real Estate Agents Authority supervises real estate agents, brokers, dealers, valuers and developers (appointed 16/08/2023 per Act 2023; FIU page footnote says agents are still under GRA pending transition). GRA real-estate house-agent annual licence G$32,500. Tax Practice Certificate for accountants and lawyers renewed 1 Jan to 28 Feb. All of this sits inside K03's buyer group; nothing new beyond K03 except the regime change.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guyana Tourism Authority Act and Tourism Accommodation Establishments Regulations 2008 cover hotels, apartments, guest houses (2+ bedrooms) and inns; licence needs EPA and Chief Environmental Health Officer reports. GTA online licensing portal since Aug 2022; about 235 local tourism businesses, 88% registered, move to licensing announced (Stabroek, about March 2026). No tourism levy found. Small market. Candidate C06 (weak).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber legality is K06 and customs single window is K05, both rejected. GRDB rice export licensing found (see 22). Gold export chain is covered by C04/C05. Nothing new for fish or food in the searches run (no search spent specifically on fish/seafood export; marked unchecked).

coverage.category: 31. Gold dealers, traders and exporters (Guyana Gold Board, GGMC trader licences)
coverage.found: Only holders of a Gold Board dealer licence or GGMC trader licence may buy gold; official receipt books for traders; ministry announced stricter audits of purchase records, source-declaration checks and licence sanctions after 10 Dec 2025 meeting; about 30+ to 70 licensed traders, 4 exporters, 6 Gold Board offices; cash limit raised to G$6m. Dealers under AML (cash transactions of $2m or more). Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 32. Gaming: casinos, betting shops, lotteries (Gaming Authority)
coverage.found: Gaming Authority Bill 2026 (Bill No. 12 of 2026) tabled July 2026 for licensing, supervision, taxation of casinos, gaming lounges, betting shops, betting shop agents, remote gaming; includes AML duties and a Responsible Gaming Fund. Not confirmed passed. Gaming Authority already supervises betting shops, casinos, lotteries under AML Act; GRA tax on bets with returns. Candidate C09.

coverage.category: 33. Weights and measures: trade scales, pumps, meters (GNBS legal metrology)
coverage.found: Weights and Measures Act 1981: all trade measuring instruments verified twice yearly by GNBS (scales, masses, tanks, flow meters, petrol pumps); August 2026 second-half round under way; seizures and prosecution for unverified instruments. Tens of thousands of vendors but low willingness to pay; reminder or booking service only. Candidate C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 34. Data Protection Act 2023 (registration, DPO, impact assessments)
coverage.found: Act No. 18 of 2023 assented 16 Aug 2023; reported as not in force as of 2026 (no commencement order found), Data Protection Office not established. Would require data controller registration. Watch item; candidate C11 (unverified).

coverage.category: 35. Fire safety and petroleum certificates (Guyana Fire Service)
coverage.found: Fire Prevention Act Cap 22:01; fire safety certificate renewal ignored by many businesses (2018 Chief Fire Prevention Officer). GFS certificate is a prerequisite for GRA/GEA petroleum, pharmacy and other licences. No current GFS portal or fee data found; folded into C01 and C12.

coverage.category: 36. GRA annual trade licences and fiscal returns (licence renewal calendar)
coverage.found: GRA issues annual licences (gas station, pharmacy, house agent, others) with prerequisites from other agencies; VAT monthly returns due 21st for taxable turnover above G$15m (third-party source, unverified). No evidence of e-invoicing or fiscal-device mandate in Guyana. Payroll/VAT filing already covered by K04. Candidate C12.

result.competitor: I found no product for Guyana. The state portal (portal.gov.gy, 'Private security application') lists the licence as in person only, run by the Guyana Police Force, with no published steps, fees or requirements and no online renewal. Foreign guard-management tools (GuardsPro, Guardso, SecurityTime, Connecteam) handle rostering, guard tours and payroll. None mentions Guyana's licence, register or police-clearance requirements, but they could take the operations side of the market. Guard payroll and the national insurance (NIS) side are crowded by K04.
result.duty: The licensing duty is real. Guyana's Private Security Services Act 2009 makes the Commissioner of Police the Controlling Authority. Nobody may run a private security service without his licence. The 2009 bill's section list covers renewal and cancellation of licences, registers and accounts the agencies must keep, guard photo-ID cards and uniforms, and penalties. In 2016 the government's news agency (DPI) reported that licences are renewed yearly, that the Minister wanted new checks at each renewal, and that police do random compliance checks. In February 2023 the Ministry of Home Affairs (MoHA) said all security services must be certified by the Police Academy. I could not check the enacted wording, penalty amounts or what the register must contain: the bill PDF returned a 404, and I found no consolidated Act online.
result.market: The market is very small. No official count of licensed firms was found. The industry association GAPSO has about 17 members, both contract firms and in-house security services, covering roughly 4,500 officers (Stabroek News, likely March 2026). My estimate of the whole licensed sector is a few dozen to perhaps 100–150 firms, mostly small, with demand growing from the oil and gas sector. That estimate is not verified.
result.reason: The duty looks real: a police licence, yearly renewal, registers and guard ID, with Police Academy certification added in 2023. No Guyana-specific tool exists, and the government licence process is in person only. But the buyer pool is tiny: GAPSO has about 17 members and the whole sector is perhaps under 150 firms. Annual renewal is low-frequency pain. The register and clearance features overlap with general guard-management SaaS such as GuardsPro and SecurityTime, and payroll/NIS is crowded. Willingness to pay for a narrow compliance pack is doubtful. It would need to be bundled with rostering to be worth buying, which pushes it into generic-tool territory. Selling through GAPSO is easy, but revenue potential is low.

result.competitor: The GGMC E-Services portal (eservices.ggmc.gov.gy) has offered gold declaration since May 2025, though the announcement was aimed at goldsmiths. It also issues invoices, takes third-party payments and links to an ArcGIS mineral-tenure map. Dredge registration still appears to use a paper form; I could not confirm whether it can be done online. Declaration mostly happens when gold is sold to the Gold Board or licensed traders, who record it. I found no private software, but I only searched in English, which is the local language.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. Section 206A of Guyana's Mining Regulations requires every dredge or specified-machinery owner to register it with the GGMC Commissioner. A dredge licence needs that registration certificate, and owners must tell the GGMC about later equipment changes. In January 2026 President Ali ordered that registered dredges with no 2025 gold declaration be deregistered. The GGMC then suspended all operations and approvals of named non-compliant miners, and some foreign miners face prosecution and expulsion. Gold is declared continuously through GGMC offices, officials visiting mining districts on set days, the Guyana Gold Board and more than 30 licensed traders (GGMC, Aug 2026). I did not find fixed fine amounts.
result.market: The latest count I found is 1,132 dredges registered and operating as of December 2018, from a GGMC-based overview. I found no 2025 figure. In 2018 small and medium-scale mines produced 58.5% of gold output. The market is probably a few thousand operators, many in remote interior areas with limited internet, and some are informal or foreign (Brazilian) operators.
result.reason: The duty is real and enforcement is sharp after the January 2026 order: deregistration and suspensions. But the core job, declaring gold, happens when it is sold through the Gold Board, licensed traders and GGMC officials, and the state's E-Services portal already offers online declaration. A private tracker would only add reminders and record-keeping for dredge registration and licence renewals, which is low value. Buyers are hard to reach (interior, cash-based, partly informal or foreign, poor connectivity), and willingness to pay for software is doubtful. The market is small, about 1,100 dredges in 2018. Selling through the GGDMA (the miners' association) is possible but narrow. I didn't refute the idea because nothing does a full compliance tracker, but the opportunity is weak.

Duty is real: the Old Metal Dealers Act (Cap 91:08) requires dealer registration and licensing, a register to be kept, a signboard, inspection, and Minister-controlled export suspension. The 2006 amendment added export offences. Enforcement is now by the Ministry of Tourism, Industry and Commerce and its Scrap Metal Unit. Sept 2026 warnings threaten licence cancellation. I could not read the PDF text, so frequency, fees and penalties are unverified. I found no Guyanese software, app or e-register, and no licensed-dealer count. The market is likely tiny, perhaps dozens of firms. Willingness to pay is doubtful, and the trade may be shut down or reshaped. The register duty is the only recurring workflow, and it is thin. Weak as a business.

The duty is real. The Pesticides and Toxic Chemicals Control Act Cap 68:09, Part IV, covers product registration (s11), licences to manufacture, import or export (s12), licences to sell (s13) and premises registration for storage (s14). The PTCCB enforces it and the Ministry of Agriculture site says vendors must be certified. I found no software, app or online portal for it. The market is tiny: no dealer count was found, and the 2018 annual report returned 403. Renewal cycle and fees were not found. The duty looks like an occasional paper licence with no heavy recurring returns, and I did not confirm any recurring filings. A buyer base of perhaps dozens to a few hundred shops, with weak pain and weak willingness to pay, makes this a poor SaaS target.

The licensing duty exists. Recruiting of Workers Act Cap 98:06 bars recruiting without a licence and requires prescribed security. The 2021 Guyana Chronicle article says the Labour Ministry was building a register and that no agency had registered with the CRMA. I found no periodic reporting or placement-record filing duty, no stated penalty, and no 2024-2026 rule changes. I found no competing software, but the duty is a one-off or renewal licence, not a recurring workflow. The market is probably tens of agencies, I found no count, and willingness to pay looks low. The need for software is weak.

Duty is real: Childcare and Development Services Act 2011 with Regulations in force 4 May 2016. Providers must register with the Childcare and Protection Agency, then be licensed. They need police clearance, food handler's and medical certificates, and Fire, CH&PA and Public Health inspections. I found no renewal cycle, fee or penalty in my two searches. I found no online registration or competing software. The process looks paper-based, with in-person visits to the Brickdam office. The market is small, at about 700 facilities. Most are informal, and owners pay little. Distribution is hard. The state is likely to run its own system. The pain is low-frequency, so it is only a thin MVP, such as a certificate-expiry tracker.

Duty is real: only a GGB dealer licence or GGMC trader licence permits buying gold. In Dec 2025 the MNR announced stricter audits of purchasing records, source-declaration verification and routine checks, with suspension or revocation for failures (DPI). No competing software or state portal found; a 2023 plan for an online declaration platform has no confirmed launch. The market is tiny: an undated MNR page says GGB has 9 dealers, and GGMC trader numbers were not found. No fixed filing frequency or form was found, so this is audit-readiness rather than a recurring filing. Buyers are few and politically sensitive, and a government platform could displace the product. Low score.

Duty partly real. The Steam Boilers Regulation Act (Cap. 95:04, Act 22 of 1970) issues an annual licence per boiler only after examination and certification. The Chief Factories Officer keeps the register. The OSH Act (Act 32 of 1997, cited as Cap. 99:06, not 99:10) has a Part II on registering industrial establishments. Annual re-registration rests only on a 2019 DPI quote from an OSH consultant, and I found no statute text, fee schedule or enforcement data. I found no competing software. Market size is unknown: no count of establishments or boilers. Few boiler owners, a paper-based government process, small buyers and an ILO-backed OSH Act reform make this a thin, low-WTP niche.
